glossary.definition: A chunk of text the model reads or generates; billing and context limits are counted in tokens.
glossary.de_analogy: Like rows or bytes processed—your cost and SLA driver.

glossary.definition: Maximum tokens the model can consider in one request (prompt + completion).
glossary.de_analogy: Like a max batch size—overflow means truncate, summarize, or chunk.

glossary.definition: Running a trained model to produce outputs (not training).
glossary.de_analogy: Running a scoring job in prod vs retraining the model.

glossary.definition: Model output that looks plausible but is factually wrong or unsupported.
glossary.de_analogy: Bad join or null handling that still returns a row—never trust without validation.

glossary.definition: Forcing LLM responses into a schema (JSON/Pydantic) instead of free text.
glossary.de_analogy: Contract-first API response types and schema enforcement.

glossary.definition: Python library for data validation and settings using type hints.
glossary.de_analogy: Runtime schema checks like Great Expectations on a single record.

glossary.definition: Library that pairs LLM calls with Pydantic models and retries on validation failure.
glossary.de_analogy: Retry loop around a flaky API until the payload passes JSON schema.

glossary.definition: Gateway that routes requests to many model providers with one API.
glossary.de_analogy: API gateway + provider failover for model endpoints.

glossary.definition: Central entry for models: auth, routing, budgets, logging, fallbacks.
glossary.de_analogy: Kong/Apigee-style layer before downstream services.

glossary.definition: Fixed labeled examples (input → expected output) used to score changes.
glossary.de_analogy: Fixture tables in dbt tests or regression datasets.

glossary.definition: Scripts/CI that run the golden set and report metrics on every change.
glossary.de_analogy: pytest + data diff job in CI.

glossary.definition: Business rule beyond JSON shape (e.g. balances sum to zero).
glossary.de_analogy: Custom SQL tests or domain constraints.

glossary.definition: Time to first token—latency until the model starts streaming output.
glossary.de_analogy: Time-to-first-byte on an API response.

glossary.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant docs, then answer with the model.
glossary.de_analogy: Join to a reference table before computing a metric.

glossary.definition: Vector representation of text used for similarity search.
glossary.de_analogy: Feature vector for fuzzy matching instead of exact keys.

glossary.definition: Framework for agent workflows as graphs with state and checkpoints.
glossary.de_analogy: Airflow DAG with per-run state and human approval nodes.

glossary.definition: Persisted graph state so a run can resume after failure or interrupt.
glossary.de_analogy: Idempotent checkpoint in Spark/Flink or workflow saga state.

glossary.definition: Human-in-the-loop: pause automation for review before continuing.
glossary.de_analogy: Manual approval step in a pipeline.

glossary.definition: System that plans steps and calls tools; not just one LLM prompt.
glossary.de_analogy: Orchestrated micro-jobs with side effects—not a single SQL statement.

glossary.definition: Model Context Protocol—standard way to expose tools and resources to models.
glossary.de_analogy: Internal tool catalog + OpenAPI for agents.

glossary.definition: JSON schema describing parameters an agent tool accepts.
glossary.de_analogy: API request body contract.

glossary.definition: Append-only record of who invoked which tool with what outcome.
glossary.de_analogy: CloudTrail / data access logs for compliance.

glossary.definition: Metric got worse vs baseline on the golden set after a change.
glossary.de_analogy: CI test failure on main metrics.

glossary.definition: Secondary model or provider used when the primary fails or is slow.
glossary.de_analogy: Secondary region or read replica failover.

glossary.definition: How the model picks the next token (temperature, top-p).
glossary.de_analogy: Random seed / tie-break policy—lower temperature = more deterministic.

glossary.definition: Mechanism for the model to weigh which input tokens matter for each output token.
glossary.de_analogy: Weighted join keys—without math depth, just “focus mechanism.”
